title_en: He Cunde, Li Qingyu, Wang Yuhua — theft and harboring stolen goods

full_text_en:
He Cunde, Li Qingyu, Wang Yuhua — theft and harboring stolen goods case

Defendant: He Cunde, male, 36 years old, native of Chang'an County, Shaanxi Province, residing at No. 25, Village 3, Heping Road, Yumen City, Gansu Province, unemployed; convicted of theft in 1981 and corruption in 1985, sentenced to two years' and four years' imprisonment respectively, released upon completion of sentence in 1988; arrested on June 19, 1989.

Defendant: Li Qingyu, male, 21 years old, formerly a worker at Yumen Light Industrial Machinery Factory, Gansu Province; arrested on June 20, 1989.

Defendant: Wang Yuhua, female, 24 years old, formerly a worker at Yumen Light Industrial Machinery Factory, Gansu Province; arrested on June 17, 1989.

The Jiuquan Branch of Gansu Provincial People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against defendants He Cunde and Li Qingyu for theft and against defendant Wang Yuhua for harboring stolen goods before the Jiuquan Intermediate People's Court. The court formed a collegial panel according to law and, after public trial, found the following facts:

Around New Year's Day 1989, defendants He Cunde and Li Qingyu, after secret planning, decided to steal frescoes from the Dunhuang Mogao Grottoes. On the morning of January 6, 1989, He Cunde and Li Qingyu, carrying tools including a hand drill, screwdriver, and multi-purpose electrician's knife, took a bus from Yumen City to Dunhuang City. At approximately 10:00 p.m. that evening, the two defendants rode two stolen bicycles to Cave 465 in the northern area of the Mogao Grottoes. By picking locks and digging holes, they entered the cave and stole and removed three sections of frescoes: "Ming Wang (Wrathful Deity) and Attendant Bodhisattva," "Ming Wang," and "Heavenly King," with dimensions of 44×48 cm, 52×38 cm, and 71.5×90 cm respectively. The next morning, the two defendants abandoned the stolen bicycles and returned to Yumen City by bus.

Defendants He Cunde and Li Qingyu were dissatisfied with the stolen frescoes. Therefore, on January 12, 1989, they again brought their tools to Dunhuang City, stole two more bicycles, rode to the Mogao Grottoes, and entered the inner chamber of Cave 465 through the previously dug hole. They cut and stole five sections of frescoes: "Ming Wang and Attendant Bodhisattva" and "Ming Wang" with dimensions of 44×48 cm, 22×27 cm, 18×18 cm, 15×18 cm, and 42×46 cm. One piece measuring 42×46 cm fell and shattered during the cutting. Thereafter, the two defendants stored the stolen frescoes outside the cave and went to commercial outlets near the cave, where they successively pried open the doors of three tourist and painting-calligraphy shops operated by Lü Xiulan, Zhang Chunying, and Zhao Defeng, as well as the art storeroom of the Dunhuang Academy, stealing Feitian (apsara) painting albums, various color paintings, oil paintings, embroideries, rubbings, round fans, men's and women's undershirts, and various silk scarves, with a total value of RMB 11,897.46. They then buried one piece of fresco in a sand pile and carried the other frescoes and items back to Yumen City.

In February 1989, defendants He Cunde and Li Qingyu buried the stolen frescoes and other stolen goods in the Gobi Desert on the outskirts of Yumen City. During this period, Li Qingyu informed defendant Wang Yuhua (Li's fiancée) about the theft of the frescoes and other items. In early March, Li Qingyu and Wang Yuhua moved and reburied the hidden stolen goods.

According to the appraisal by the National Cultural Relics Appraisal Committee, the frescoes stolen by defendants He Cunde and Li Qingyu were all sections of the frescoes in Cave 465 of the Dunhuang Mogao Grottoes. Although all were recovered, the damage was severe and irreparable. Cave 465 is a representative Yuan Dynasty cave containing Tibetan Tantric paintings and is classified as a national Grade 1 protected cave. The cut and stolen frescoes are national Grade 1 cultural relics in museum collection.

The above facts are confirmed by physical evidence collected, crime scene investigation records, expert conclusions, witness testimony, and the defendants' confessions. These are sufficient for establishing the facts.

The Jiuquan Intermediate People's Court held in its trial that: Defendants He Cunde and Li Qingyu jointly committed the crime, and their conduct constituted joint intentional crime under Article 22, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the PRC. He Cunde and Li Qingyu played primary roles in the joint crime; in accordance with Article 23, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Criminal Law, both are principal offenders and shall be given heavier punishment. He Cunde and Li Qingyu, by stealing and removing and cutting frescoes, stole multiple pieces of national Grade 1 cultural relics in museum collection and a large amount of public and private property, constituting the crime of theft under Article 152 of the Criminal Law. The frescoes stolen by He Cunde and Li Qingyu are national Grade 1 cultural relics in museum collection and are rare treasures; the circumstances of the crime are especially serious and the nature especially vile. In accordance with Item 1 of Article 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Regarding the Severe Punishment of Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy, they shall be severely punished. He Cunde was a person who had been sentenced to imprisonment for a term of not less than fixed-term imprisonment in 1985; after completion of that sentence, within three years he again committed a crime punishable by fixed-term imprisonment or more. In accordance with Article 61, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, he is a recidivist and shall be given heavier punishment. Based on the facts and circumstances of the crimes of He Cunde and Li Qingyu, in accordance with Article 53, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, they shall be deprived of political rights for life. In accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law, all property illegally obtained by He Cunde and Li Qingyu shall be recovered; their own property used for the crime shall be confiscated. Defendant Wang Yuhua, knowing that Li Qingyu had stolen frescoes and public and private property, not only failed to report and expose the crime but actively helped him move and conceal the stolen goods; her conduct constituted the crime of harboring stolen goods under Article 172 of the Criminal Law.

Accordingly, on August 9, 1989, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. Defendants He Cunde and Li Qingyu are guilty of theft and are each sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life; defendant Wang Yuhua is guilty of harboring stolen goods and is sentenced to two years' imprisonment.

2. The illegal gains of defendants He Cunde and Li Qingyu shall be recovered; their own property used for the crime shall be confiscated.

After the first-instance judgment, defendant He Cunde appealed to the Gansu Provincial High People's Court on the grounds that the theft of the frescoes was premeditated and planned by a person surnamed Wei and that he had previously reported others for stealing a small-bore rifle, requesting a lighter sentence; defendant Li Qingyu appealed on the ground that the sentence was too severe.

The Gansu Provincial High People's Court held on the second instance that the original judgment had clear factual findings, reliable and sufficient evidence, correct application of law, appropriate sentencing, and lawful procedures. He Cunde's grounds of appeal were unsubstantiated and unsustainable. Li Qingyu's grounds of appeal were also unsustainable. The Adjudication Committee of the court discussed and decided, in accordance with Article 136, item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, on December 2, 1989, to rule to dismiss the appeals of appellants He Cunde and Li Qingyu and affirm the original judgment.

The Gansu Provincial High People's Court, pursuant to the provisions of the Supreme People's Court authorizing high people's courts to approve certain death penalty cases, approved the judgments of the Jiuquan Intermediate People's Court sentencing He Cunde and Li Qingyu to death for theft with deprivation of political rights for life.
